claims.name: Claim 1 — Reading
claims.description: Students can read closely and analytically to comprehend a range of literary and informational texts.

claims.name: Claim 2 — Writing
claims.description: Students can produce effective and well-grounded writing for a range of purposes and audiences.

claims.name: Claim 3 — Speaking & Listening

claims.name: Claim 4 — Research
claims.description: Students can engage in research and inquiry to investigate topics and to analyze, integrate, and present information.

claims.name: Claim 1 — Concepts & Procedures
claims.description: Students can explain and apply mathematical concepts and carry out mathematical procedures with precision and fluency.

claims.name: Claim 2 — Problem Solving
claims.description: Students can solve a range of complex, well-posed problems using appropriate mathematical tools.

claims.name: Claim 3 — Communicating Reasoning
claims.description: Students can clearly and precisely construct viable arguments to support their own reasoning.

claims.name: Claim 4 — Modeling & Data Analysis

score_points.description: Clear and effective organizational structure creating unity and completeness. Strong command of purpose throughout. Sophisticated transitions.
Adequate organizational structure. Clear introduction and conclusion. Logical development. Transitions present but may be formulaic.
Inconsistent organizational structure. Introduction or conclusion may be weak. Limited transitions.
Little or no discernible structure. No clear introduction or conclusion. Development absent or tangential.
Blank, copied text, or entirely off-task.
Convincing and thorough elaboration. Precise use of relevant evidence from sources. Effective elaborative techniques. Vocabulary precise and enhances response.
Adequate elaboration. Some use of relevant evidence. Adequate vocabulary generally appropriate to the task.
Weak or cursory elaboration. Evidence present but unelaborated or imprecise. General or imprecise vocabulary.
Minimal or no evidence from sources. Vocabulary vague or below grade level.
Blank or entirely off-task.
Consistent application of conventions with few errors. Sentence variety enhances response. Minor errors do not interfere with understanding.
Adequate command of conventions. Some errors present that do not significantly interfere with meaning.
Partial command of conventions. Errors noticeable and occasionally interfere with meaning.
Limited command of conventions. Frequent errors significantly interfere with meaning.
Blank or not enough writing to evaluate.
Accurate answer with text-based evidence that directly addresses the research question. Evidence cited or paraphrased correctly.
Partially correct answer, or correct answer with incomplete or tangential evidence.
Incorrect, insufficient, or blank.
Response demonstrates complete and correct mathematical reasoning with appropriate vocabulary. Work is clear and well-organized.
Response demonstrates partial understanding. Minor errors present or justification is incomplete.
Response is incorrect, irrelevant, or blank.
All parts correct with clear, complete mathematical reasoning. Work shown systematically.
All parts essentially correct. Minor computational or notational error.
Correct approach throughout. One significant error or one part incorrect.
Correct approach on majority of parts. Multiple minor errors or one major error.
Partial understanding. Correct approach on some parts.
Minimal understanding shown. Some relevant mathematical work.
Incorrect, irrelevant, or blank.

ELA.template_text:
Read the informational article "[PASSAGE_TITLE]" (approx. [WORD_COUNT] words, [LEXILE]L).

Part A ([STANDARD_CODE]):
What is the [main relationship / central idea / author's primary claim] presented in this article?
A. [Distractor — plausible but superficial]
B. [Distractor — partially correct, misses nuance]
C. [Correct — addresses standard precisely at DOK 2]
D. [Distractor — common misconception]

Part B:
Which sentence from the article BEST supports your answer to Part A?
A. "[Quote — does not support Part A answer]"
B. "[Quote — tangentially related]"
C. "[Quote — directly supports correct Part A answer]"
D. "[Quote — misleading surface connection]"

Answer Key: Part A: C | Part B: C
Alignment: [STANDARD_CODE] | Claim 1 | DOK 2 | [LEXILE]L

Read the passage "[PASSAGE_TITLE]".

Part A ([STANDARD_CODE]):
What is [author's argument / theme / central idea / point of view] in this text?
A. [Distractor]
B. [Distractor]
C. [Correct — requires inference and analysis at DOK 3]
D. [Distractor]

Part B:
Which detail from the passage BEST supports your answer to Part A?
A. "[Short quote — does not support Part A]"
B. "[Short quote — partially supports Part A]"
C. "[Short quote — directly supports correct Part A answer]"
D. "[Short quote — misleading]"

Answer Key: Part A: C | Part B: C
Alignment: [STANDARD_CODE] | Claim 1 | DOK 3 | [LEXILE]L

[STUDENT DIRECTION]: You have read the following sources about [TOPIC]:
- "[TITLE_1]" by [AUTHOR_1]
- "[TITLE_2]" by [AUTHOR_2]
- "[TITLE_3]" by [AUTHOR_3]

Write an argumentative essay explaining your position on [DEBATABLE ISSUE].
Use evidence from at least two of the three sources to support your argument.
Make sure to address a counterclaim in your essay.

[SCORING GUIDE — 3 traits, 0–4 each, 12 pts total]
Trait 1 — Organization/Purpose: clarity of claim, logical structure, purposeful development
Trait 2 — Evidence/Elaboration: textual evidence, elaboration quality, vocabulary
Trait 3 — Conventions: grammar, punctuation, spelling, sentence variety

Alignment: W.[GRADE].1 / RI.[GRADE].8 / RI.[GRADE].9 | Claim 2 | DOK 3–4

assessments.ELA: STAAR ELA (State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness)

ELA.notes: STAAR 2023 redesign: stacked passages with multiple items per stimulus. Mix of MCQ, Short Answer (SA), and Revising/Editing items.

ELA.name: Stacked Multiple Choice
ELA.description: Multiple MCQ items sharing one stimulus (passage or paired passages). Each question is 1 point. Students read one passage then answer 4-8 questions about it.
ELA.example_stem: Which sentence from the passage BEST shows the character's internal conflict?

ELA.name: Short Answer
ELA.description: Brief written response (2-4 sentences) scored 0, 1, or 2. Student must provide text evidence.
ELA.example_stem: Using evidence from the passage, explain how the author develops the theme of perseverance.

ELA.name: Extended Response — Personal Narrative
ELA.description: Multi-paragraph personal narrative scored on Organization, Development, Voice, and Conventions. Scored 0–4 per trait.
ELA.example_stem: Write about a time when you overcame a challenge. Use specific details to develop your story.

ELA.name: Extended Response — Expository
ELA.description: Multi-paragraph expository essay scored on Organization, Development, Voice, and Conventions.
ELA.example_stem: Explain how facing challenges can make people stronger. Use specific examples to develop your essay.

ELA.name: Revising and Editing
ELA.description: Items embedded in a student-written draft passage. Students identify errors or suggest improvements.
ELA.example_stem: Which revision BEST improves the underlined sentence in paragraph 3?
